title: Uncommitted ICD10CM regex tightening rejects every 3-character code (I10, E11, F10, N18) — do not commit as-is
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while reconciling this repo's long-stale working tree. The uncommitted changes are
NOT inert cleanup — they tighten three regexes, and one of them is an outright correctness
regression against the rule this repo's README calls non-negotiable.

## The regression
  committed:    ICD10CM  ^\w{3}.?\w{0,4}$      (dot OPTIONAL, any-char)
  uncommitted:  ICD10CM  ^\w{3}\.\w{0,4}$       (dot REQUIRED, literal)

Tested against real codes:
  I10    PASS -> FAIL      essential hypertension
  E11    PASS -> FAIL      type 2 diabetes
  F10    PASS -> FAIL      alcohol related disorders
  N18    PASS -> FAIL      chronic kidney disease
  I63.9 / E11.9 / M05.79 / U07.1 / Z3A.01   PASS -> PASS

Three-character ICD-10-CM codes are REAL and valid, and in the OHDSI concept table they are stored
in the dotted vocabulary WITH NO DOT — verified against the June-2026 Athena build
(concept_code is dotted for ICD9CM/ICD10CM: I63.9, 433.01; 3-char roots have no dot). So requiring
a literal dot makes the dotted regex reject a large, common class of genuine codes.

That is precisely the failure mode the README forbids: 'skewed toward valid... tolerate a few false
positives, NEVER reject a real code. False negatives unacceptable.' Recorded as a hard constraint in
seed vfm-6oo and in bead vocabulary_formats-3h8.

## The other two changes — defensible, but same direction
  HCPCS                 ^\w\d{4}$          -> ^[A-V]\d{4}$
  HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS   ^(\w\d{4}|\w{2})$  -> ^([A-V]\d{4}|[A-X]\w)$
Accurate for TODAY's HCPCS Level II letter range, but it is still a tightening in a repo whose whole
posture is permissiveness, and it goes stale the moment CMS allocates outside A-V. Compare the
README's own COVID U-code cautionary tale. Decide deliberately rather than inheriting.

## Why this sat unnoticed
The working tree has been dirty since roughly 2026-02 (README.md and the TSV modified; CLAUDE.md,
Makefile and the parquet untracked), with no seeds or beads in the repo to record intent. Whoever
made the edits left no note, and nothing consumed the file strictly enough to fail.

## What to do
1. REVERT the ICD10CM change, or split it: keep the dotted regex permissive and let ICD10CM.DOTLESS
   handle the undotted form (it already does: ^\w{3,7}$). If the intent was to make the two
   variants mutually exclusive, that is a DIFFERENT and larger design change — it would break the
   'either variant matches' contract consumers rely on, and lit-et6.1's dotted-code-trap finding
   warns that a consumer reading one variant silently under-counts.
2. Decide the HCPCS tightening on its merits and write the reasoning into the notes column.
3. Regenerate the parquet (make all) so it cannot drift from the TSV — the untracked parquet is
   currently a 2024 artifact.
4. Reconcile the untracked CLAUDE.md and Makefile.

Do this BEFORE vocabulary_formats-3h8 (extend regexes to non-claims vocabs) adds rows on top of an
unreviewed base.

Related: vfm-6oo (the permissive-regex constraint), vocabulary_formats-3h8, vocabulary_formats-e5s.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-07-25 per Ryan's ruling: for ICD10, handle 3-character codes in BOTH dotted and dotless variants; for dotted, if the code is longer than four characters the fourth position must be a dot. ICD10CM becomes ^\w{3}(\.\w{1,4})?$ — the optional group means a 3-char code needs no dot, and when the group fires position 4 is a literal dot followed by 1-4 characters. ICD10CM.DOTLESS unchanged (^\w{3,7}$ already admits 3-char; max real undotted length is exactly 7). The two HCPCS tightenings were reverted on evidence, not preference: [A-V] rejects X1002, a real 5-character HCPCS code, while ^\w\d{4}$ misses none of the 12,179. Validated through the regenerated parquet against the June-2026 Athena build: 0 false negatives on 100,035 ICD10CM codes (dotted and dotless) and 0 on HCPCS. The broken pattern it replaced had 1,953 (1.95%).

title: Add the vocab-label id-normalization REGISTRY table (verbatim label -> OHDSI vocabulary_id, blank = unsupported)
description:
From seed vfm-31w (decided by Ryan across litmine's lit-et6.1, 2026-07-23 refinement + 2026-07-24
registry framing; filed here 2026-07-25).

## What to build
A SECOND table alongside the format regexes: an ID-normalization map from a vocabulary label 'hit in
the wild' -> a known-good OHDSI vocabulary_id.
  'ICD-10-CM'    -> ICD10CM
  WHO 'ICD-10'   -> ICD10
  'CPT' / 'CPT-4'-> CPT4

## It is a REGISTRY, not just a mapping — this is the load-bearing part
Every vocabulary label encountered is recorded VERBATIM, and each row resolves to EITHER a known-good
OHDSI vocabulary_id OR a **BLANK** id meaning 'not supported in OHDSI (as of now)'.

Ryan: 'if the vocab doesn't exist, we record it as it appears in the literature into that mapping file
and either derive a mapping or leave the mapping with no OHDSI ID to indicate that the vocab isn't
supported in OHDSI.'

Consequences that make the blank column worth the trouble:
- The table becomes the COMPLETE registry of labels seen + their OHDSI status. One source of truth.
- **A blank id IS litmine's non-OMOP gate** (lit-et6.3's extract-but-don't-produce set). No separate
  list needs maintaining.
- Provenance preserved (verbatim label is the key) and omission is VISIBLE — a blank loudly marks
  'not in OHDSI' instead of a code set silently vanishing (habitat rule 7).
- Blank means 'unsupported AS OF NOW' — revisitable when OHDSI or an OI supplemental vocab adds it.

## Seed data to build it from
- litmine's pilot produced **22 distinct vocabulary labels for ~14 real vocabularies** across 380
  code sets — that is the initial population, and it is real evidence rather than a guess.
- code_collector's vocab_mappings.csv (21 rows, name -> OHDSI id) eventually MIGRATES here.

## Constraints
- Keep this repo DATA-ONLY and polyglot. The consuming code lives in codesistant (cst-*), which reads
  both tables. Adding Python here would break the language-neutral value that is the whole point.
- 'Permissive' does NOT apply to this table — it is a plain lookup, not a regex.
- Keyed to the format regexes by OHDSI vocabulary_id.

## Downstream
Its non-blank ids can populate litmine's extraction-time vocabulary enum (lit-et6.4), which keeps the
enum and the format regexes from drifting apart. Build the enum FROM THIS DATA, not from a guess —
litmine's 'exposure' precedent (3rd-commonest role label, absent from the hand-written list) is the
cautionary case.

## Authoring
Hand the mappings to a domain agent — Odie (OHDSI/OMOP) or Vincent (vocab) or the vocabulary habitat.

## Before starting
Repo has stale uncommitted changes (see the sibling regex bead); reconcile them first.

title: Extend format regexes to litmine's non-claims vocabularies (WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD10PCS, ATC, DRG, ICD-O-3)
description:
From seed vfm-6oo (decided by Ryan in litmine's lit-et6.1, 2026-07-23; filed here 2026-07-25).

## The gap
The table is 13 rows covering CLAIMS vocabularies only (ICD9CM, ICD10CM, HCPCS, CPT4, NDC + their
.DOTLESS / modifier / .ALPHANUM variants). litmine extracts code sets in whatever vocabulary a paper
used, so it needs rows for WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD10PCS, ATC, DRG, ICD-O-3, and whatever else
the corpus turns up. Ryan: 'tens of rows at most', cheap.

## HARD CONSTRAINT — keep them PERMISSIVE
Per this repo's README the regexes are deliberately skewed toward valid: accept anything that COULD
be a valid code, tolerate false positives, NEVER reject a real code. **False negatives are
unacceptable** (hence the loose ICD10CM \\w{3}.\\w{0,4} so future U-codes still pass).

Do NOT attempt strict/existence validation here. A regex validates FORMAT; it cannot validate
EXISTENCE — that is set-membership, answered only by the concept DB. You can't pattern your way to
'E11.9 is real but E11.99 is not', and a tight regex goes stale as codes change yearly.

The two layers together classify failures on different axes, which is more useful than either alone:
passes-format-but-misses-DB = well-formed but not real (typo / retired / non-US variant);
fails-format = malformed. That is litmine's validate.py taxonomy, already in production.

## Two field-tested constraints to inherit rather than rediscover
1. THE DOTTED-CODE TRAP — an undotted-only regex truncates 'M05.79' to category 'M05', collapsing a
   338-code list to ~12 hits. Every vocabulary needs BOTH forms covered. A consumer reading only one
   variant silently UNDER-COUNTS rather than erroring.
2. A >=4-CHARACTER FLOOR belongs in the CALLER, not here. It stops bare 3-char categories in disease
   prose ('F10', 'I21') matching during a scan — but a real 3-char code like 'I10' is legitimately
   valid, so putting the floor in the format regex would create exactly the false negative this repo
   forbids. Worth stating in the README as the regexes gain consumers; it is the kind of rule that
   gets pushed down into the shared layer by mistake.

## Mechanics
Edit vocabulary_formats.tsv; 'make all' regenerates the parquet. Keyed by OHDSI vocabulary_id, which
is also the join key to the id-normalization registry.

## Authoring
Hand the new regexes to a domain agent — Odie (OHDSI/OMOP) or Vincent (vocab) or the vocabulary
habitat — to author and validate. Do not guess them.

## Before starting
The repo has uncommitted changes (README.md, vocabulary_formats.tsv) plus untracked CLAUDE.md /
Makefile / vocabulary_formats.parquet, all with stale mtimes (2024 - 2026-02). Reconcile those first.
